commits.edited_message:
Right-size the QuickTime tag buffers

decodeBlock() grew its tag buffer to the full atom size even though the
buffer only ever holds the four-byte atom name that tagDecoder()
dispatches on, so the resize did nothing.

audioDescDecoder() walks the sound description in four-byte chunks into
a nul-terminated tag buffer but was still allocating 40 bytes for it;
five is enough for a chunk plus the terminator.

Nul-terminate strings, decode v1 sound description fields

previewTagDecoder(), keysTagDecoder(), CameraTagsDecoder(),
imageDescDecoder(), handlerDecoder() and isQTimeType() passed
four-byte tag chunks to string constructors and table lookups without
a terminator; write the nul explicitly and size the buffers to match
instead of relying on stale memset zeros.

audioDescDecoder() now also decodes the samples-per-packet and
bytes-per-packet pair that version 1 sound descriptions append after
the version 0 fields, reading the two 32-bit values as one block.

coupling: The defect is a producer/consumer split over one shared buffer, QuickTimeVideo::audioDescDecoder()'s tag buffer in src/quicktimevideo.cpp. Commit 4cdd0e5 (rewritten as 'Right-size the QuickTime tag buffers') shrinks that buffer from DataBuf buf(40) to DataBuf buf(5): four bytes for one chunk of the sound-description walk plus the nul terminator the walk writes. In that commit's own tree the shrink is provably safe - every read the function performs is at most four bytes, and the buffer is never used for anything longer. Commit da1b3e8 (rewritten as 'Nul-terminate strings, decode v1 sound description fields') later teaches the same function to decode the version-1 sound description extension: a new case AudioV1Extension that reads the samples-per-packet / bytes-per-packet pair as one 8-byte block with io_->readOrThrow(buf.data(), 8). Against the 40-byte buffer the function had when that feature code is written, an 8-byte read is comfortably in bounds and the diff is correct maintenance; against the 5-byte buffer sized by the earlier commit it overflows the heap allocation by three bytes (heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8 in MemIo::read's memcpy, reached through ImageFactory::open + Image::readMetadata). Neither diff alone is wrong and neither contains both the too-small size and the too-large read: commit 1's diff shows only a shrink that is locally justified by every read visible in its tree (max 4), and commit 2's diff shows only a read that never touches the size. A correct fix must reconcile the two - either bound the read by the buffer commit 1 sized, or resize the buffer to the read commit 2 added (8 bytes plus terminator) - which requires reasoning across both commits; validating either commit in isolation leaves its own change looking correct. Verified by execution: the tree with only commit 1's edit applied parses the probe and a real-video corpus byte-identically to the original batch; the tree with only commit 2's edit applied also parses cleanly (and gains the two new XMP tags the feature is meant to produce); only the tree with both edits aborts under AddressSanitizer.

pocs.entry_point: Exiv2::ImageFactory::open(const byte*, size_t) followed by Image::readMetadata() on an in-memory QuickTime/MOV buffer (public exiv2.hpp API; C-compatible TU compiled as C++)
